seed-input.means: type a seed, get the same result again
seed-input.why: the game takes an int seed; 1.0 takes any text

seed-url.means: seed and options in a shareable URL or code
seed-url.why: built for 1.0.0: GeneratorOptions.ToCode() and FromCode(code), Universe.Link(address, options) and links (address?code) in Universe.At; planned as: Options.ToCode() / FromCode(); the lab page's addresses (D11, D17)

seed-versioned.means: seeds carry a generator version so old ones keep working
seed-versioned.why: D4: v1-... seeds; rare among libraries, the fix for broken share links (Azgaar, watabou, Dyson Sphere Program)

hierarchical-address.means: any object regenerates alone from its address

lazy-generation.why: D16: memory follows what the game opens

presets.why: D15: SpaceOpera, Pocket, Roguelike, Plausible, Cozy, Epic

options-sliders.why: D15: every option validated with a readable message

data-tables-editable.means: users replace or extend the tables
data-tables-editable.why: D7: C# records plus JSON tables by id; ScriptableObject adapter in the Unity package

hooks-plugins.why: D7: OnSystemGenerated-style hooks and a per-object Tags dictionary

constraints.why: landmark guarantee and fair starts need it; deterministic repair pass on its own stream

explain-trace.means: show why a value is what it is
explain-trace.why: Explain() reads the rules after the fact, so it can come later

engine-neutral-data.means: plain data usable outside one engine
engine-neutral-data.why: no Unity types; float adapters in the Unity package

deterministic-cross-platform.means: documented identical output on every OS and runtime
deterministic-cross-platform.why: D5; golden tests on Windows, Linux, macOS, Mono and IL2CPP; nobody surveyed proves it

seed-search.means: search seeds for an output that matches a test
seed-search.why: FindSeeds(predicate); cheap thanks to lazy generation; players already brute-force seeds

fill-around-fixed.means: pin known facts, generate the rest to match
fill-around-fixed.why: writers start from one imagined world; a separate entry point leaves unpinned output alone

detail-levels.means: more detail never changes the major bodies
detail-levels.why: falls out of D17's per-purpose streams; Terra Invicta's model

overlay-diffs.means: player changes stored as a diff over the generated base
overlay-diffs.why: a game's job, but an Overlay type saves every user writing it

time-coordinate.means: orbital positions and seasons as functions of time

outlier-quota.means: a share of outputs may break the rules on purpose
outlier-quota.why: Weirdness slider; part of the answer to oatmeal

universe-level.why: D14; a level above never changes a galaxy (D17), so it may slip to 1.1 if the estimate is over

cluster-level.why: D14; same slip rule as the universe level

galaxy-shapes.why: prototyped: spiral, barred, elliptical, ring, irregular; add cluster, colliding pair, starburst

custom-shape-map.means: an image or density map as the shape
custom-shape-map.why: a density-function hook; image decoding stays outside the library

min-spacing.why: prototyped; the game today has neighbours 2.7 units apart

regions-sectors.why: the game has Core, MidRim, OuterRim by radius; 1.0 grows named regions over the lane graph (prototyped)

constellations.means: constellations and Bayer letters seen from home
constellations.why: a separate naming pass from a chosen home (Star Control: Origins)

lanes-graph.why: prototyped (relative neighbourhood graph plus Gabriel edges)

lane-density.why: prototyped; the extra-edge roll is drawn for every pair, so the option shifts nothing else

wormholes-gates.means: long links, gates, relays, with requirements
wormholes-gates.why: Star Ruler 2's ring of wormholes for the universe level; gate requirements (A9)

travel-terrain.means: free travel changed by terrain instead of lanes
travel-terrain.why: nebula fields on their own stream; a LaneMode option (lanes, terrain, both)

danger-levels.why: the game's 1 to 10 never reaches 10; 1.0 uses hops plus regional noise (prototyped)

radial-progression.means: difficulty or tier by distance from a centre, barrier rings

factions-territory.why: grown over the lane graph on its own stream (idea 22); story first (D18)

start-fairness.why: Starts(n) as a pass that reads the galaxy; 4X users need it

contested-richness.why: Star Ruler 2's score, applied by the start pass

nebulae-hazards.means: nebulae, storms, black holes on the map
nebulae-hazards.why: the game has Nebula and Anomaly flags, switched off; 1.0 places hazards by region

galaxy-age-metallicity.means: age and metallicity change the content
galaxy-age-metallicity.why: prototyped as region age shifting the star mix

handmade-systems.means: hand-made systems mixed into the map
handmade-systems.why: pinned systems by address (idea 25); the game's home system is the first user

run-map.why: extracted from the lane graph (idea 24); SpaceDeckBuilder2 is the first user

landmark-guarantee.means: a memorable feature at every scale
landmark-guarantee.why: the answer to oatmeal; the prototype's system sheet shows the need

spectral-classes.why: prototyped; the game has seven coarse types and never rolls blue, giant or supergiant

star-physics.why: prototyped; the game draws mass 0.8 to 2.5 for any type

star-remnants.means: white dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes, giants
star-remnants.why: the game's centres include remnants and black holes; 1.0 adds giants and supergiants

multiple-stars.why: the game names 2 and 3-body centres; 1.0 adds close or wide pairs that affect planets (prototyped)

star-age.why: region age drives giants and white dwarfs (prototyped coarsely)

planet-types.why: the game has four; prototype has 13 by zone

orbit-spacing.why: prototyped (period ratio); the game adds 1.5 to 4 units

exo-demographics.why: peas in a pod, giants past the frost line, binaries suppressing planets; cheap and must be in 1.0

orbital-elements.why: on the planet's own stream; the game has Circular or Elliptical labels only

planet-physics.why: the game draws radius, density and gravity independently; 1.0 derives them

temperature-climate.why: P10, P12 on the planet's streams

atmosphere.why: the game has profiles but never uses them; 1.0 with the Jeans rule and a why note

biomes.why: biome shares from climate (P15) on their own stream

life-ladder.means: none to sentient, flora and fauna
life-ladder.why: the game has a life flag that never fires; 1.0 has the ladder (P3)

life-conditions-table.why: condition rows for creature archetypes (Elite exobiology) on their own stream

resources.why: the game has belt deposits; 1.0 grades planets 1 to 5 by composition (P6)

moons.why: the game's code exists but no archetype allows moons; prototyped by planet kind

asteroid-belts.why: the game has belts that overlap planets 127 times in 200 systems; prototype places them in gaps

surface-map.why: a parameter pack for engines (P16), no meshes; own stream

planet-traits.why: P1, on its own stream; story first (D18)

stations.why: the game has 30 name combinations and stations orbiting planets that do not exist; 1.0 fixes both

population-society.why: optional society layer (P5) on its own stream

story-tags.means: tags with enemies, friends, complications, things, places
story-tags.why: the stand-out feature for writers (idea 21), own stream

history-events.why: generate then explain (Caves of Qud), own stream

description-text.why: tag-filtered grammar; a one-line descriptor ships in core at 1.0

gm-secrets.why: a secret per object in the text layer; a player-safe export

names-catalogue.why: the game's CelestialNaming; 1.0 keeps it with tables embedded instead of the 954 KB RandomNameGeneratorLibrary dependency

names-fantasy.why: names on their own stream, so additive

names-hierarchical.why: the game's planet letters and Roman-numeral moons

name-encodes-address.means: a name decodes to its address
name-encodes-address.why: an optional naming style (Elite boxel names)

culture-phonology.why: Syllabore (MIT, .NET Standard 2.0) as dependency or model

map-render.why: an SVG string export; the lab page draws in 1.0, the library export can follow

map-3d.why: visual, not data; the library gives 3D coordinates and engines render

export-json.why: a versioned schema, hand-written writer (no reflection, D19)

export-markdown.why: YAML properties, relative links, GM section (A3)

export-image.why: SVG only; PNG is the caller's job

export-vtt.why: journal-entry JSON after the writers' survey confirms the format

export-text-html.why: plain text sheet; HTML is the lab page's job

edit-after-generate.means: edit or lock, then regenerate the rest

godot-integration.why: Godot 4 C# takes the NuGet package; a GDScript addon is out of scope

sub-seeds.means: every object exposes its own seed or stable id
sub-seeds.why: D17: every object has Address and Seed

visited-cache.means: places are saved when first visited so later changes never alter them
visited-cache.why: versioned seeds (D4) solve it without storage; a game can still save what it wants

multiplayer-determinism.means: server and clients derive the same world from the seed
multiplayer-determinism.why: follows from D5 and the golden tests; say so in the README

determinism-tests.means: golden or hash tests in CI
determinism-tests.why: D4, D5: Windows, Linux, macOS, Mono, IL2CPP

typed-units.why: D16: Units option (game units, AU, ly, pc) on plain doubles; no UnitsNet dependency (size)

diagnostics.means: soft problems returned as typed warnings
diagnostics.why: D15: Validate() and budget trims report what changed

cited-assumptions.means: each assumption shown with its source
cited-assumptions.why: the wiki's rules pages cite every formula; Explain() can link them

custom-fields.means: users add, rename or hide fields

rpg-system-profiles.means: generation biased by a tabletop rule set
rpg-system-profiles.why: Traveller UWP and SWN tags as presets and exports; rules text not copied

real-star-catalogue.size: tens to hundreds of KB, outside core
real-star-catalogue.why: Mark 2026-10-03 reverses the 2026-10-02 rejection in a bounded form: larger catalogues (10 pc census, Gaia nearby stars) go to an add-on, a small nearest-stars table to core; licences first (ai-docs/notes/2026-10-03-real-stars-track.md); was rejected: game and fiction scale (D16, D18); catalogue data is large; a hand-made-systems hook covers a few real stars

connected-graph.why: the relative neighbourhood graph is connected (prototyped)

spatial-index.means: query what is in a cell
spatial-index.why: a grid index over positions; additive

pathfinding-routes.why: Route(a, b) by breadth-first search or A*; additive

visibility-helpers.why: game logic, not generation; the lane graph and positions give a game what it needs

galaxy-blend.why: density functions compose (Gaia Sky channels); colliding pair ships in 1.0

comets.why: minor bodies on their own detail stream

sky-view.means: what the sky looks like from the surface
sky-view.why: apparent size and colour of suns and moons, derived; the gap writers noticed

local-calendar.means: day, year and seasons as a calendar

npcs.why: characters belong to RandomNameGeneratorLibrary or the game; the library gives culture and name hooks

entity-links.why: addresses are links; factions, lanes and neighbours reference addresses

llm-text.means: prose written by a language model
llm-text.why: non-deterministic, needs a service; tag-filtered grammar instead. A caller can still feed our data to a model

history-log.why: the lab page keeps recent seeds in the browser

share-gallery.why: seed URLs are shareable; a gallery is a site feature for later

player-view-live.why: a VTT's or site's job; the player-safe export feeds it

export-traveller-map.why: needs the profile code; a reach into an active community

export-wiki-site.why: a folder of Markdown files is the route (LegendKeeper, Foundry MD to Journal)

export-wiki-tool.means: export shaped for a wiki app
export-wiki-tool.why: World Anvil and Kanka imports are closed or paid; Markdown first

import-foreign.why: a generator, not a converter; hand-made systems take our own JSON

editor-preview.why: a Gizmos sample in Samples~ at 1.0; an editor window later

dice-tables-printable.why: the wiki can print the tables for table play

pinned-systems.means: place hand-made or real systems into a generated map
pinned-systems.why: Mark 2026-10-03 (real stars track): the hook every real-data feature needs; a pinned star and known planets, the rest generated around them

real-neighbourhood.means: a map of the real stars around Sol
real-neighbourhood.why: Mark 2026-10-03: the nearest real systems with real positions, classes, companions and names, unknowns generated from the seed; research first (ai-docs/notes/2026-10-03-real-stars-track.md)

real-exoplanets.why: Mark 2026-10-03: Proxima b, epsilon Eridani b and the rest keep their known orbits; generated planets fill the gaps

real-and-generated.means: real stars near home, generated ones far away
real-and-generated.why: Mark 2026-10-03: Elite Dangerous's model; a generated or Milky Way galaxy with Sol's neighbourhood at home

milky-way-preset.means: an approximation of the Milky Way
milky-way-preset.why: Mark 2026-10-03: a barred spiral with its real arms and the Sun's place; tens of numbers, not a star field

real-local-group.means: the real Local Group as a cluster
real-local-group.why: Mark 2026-10-03: the Milky Way, Andromeda, Triangulum, the Magellanic Clouds and the dwarfs (about 80 rows)
